title: DiffGuardian — Understand Code as Fast as Agents Write It
excerpt: Get a spoken walkthrough of any PR or codebase and understand AI-written code as fast as agents write it. A desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux.

Talk to your PR

Get a live walkthrough of any PR, out loud, right now.

Hold Space and ask what a PR does. DiffGuardian walks you through it as it goes: the features it ships, what each one changes, what it touches. You hear it while the code it's explaining scrolls into view and lights up. Ask a follow-up whenever you like.

  • Instant. No setup per PR. Ask and it starts talking.
  • Live. The code it's explaining is highlighted and scrolled into view as it talks.
  • Yours to steer. Ask for the part you care about first, or skip straight to the one file that matters to you.

Pro. Runs on your own OpenAI or ElevenLabs key, or your system's built-in voice.

Talk to your codebase

Ask the whole repo a question. Hear the walkthrough. See it on a live graph.

DiffGuardian, available on macOS, Windows and Linux, indexes your repo into a code knowledge graph. Hold Space and ask how auth works or where a webhook is verified. It answers out loud while a live visual of the flow builds on screen, straight from your call graph.

Trace It

Prefer to read? Trace It gives you the walkthrough at your pace.

Hit Trace It! and a 5,000-line PR becomes a guided tour, one feature at a time, each explained in plain English. Read it as slowly as you like, go back, and approve having seen the whole thing, not skimmed a diff.

  • Walkthrough, written — the PR broken into the features it ships, each explained in plain English
  • Blast radius — a dependency graph built from the diff alone (heuristic, not AI): every file and module a change actually touches, before it merges

Want it spoken instead? Talk to your PR.

Built for parallel agents

Ten agents, forty PRs. You still know what's shipping.

When agents work in parallel, the bottleneck is you. For every PR, DiffGuardian finds the quickest way for you to understand it, so you spend minutes on each one instead of reading every line or rubberstamping it.

  • Knowledge bases stay on your machine, and credentials sit in your OS keychain

Questions

Your questions, answered.

What does DiffGuardian actually do?

DiffGuardian helps engineers, PMs and anyone building software

understand code as fast as agents write it. It gives you a walkthrough of a pull request one feature at a time, lets you talk to a PR or your whole codebase and hear the answer, and leaves the decision to approve with you.

Can I really talk to a PR?

Yes. On the PR page, hold Space, ask, release, and hear the answer while the lines it discusses are highlighted. Analyze Project has the same push-to-talk in a full-screen overlay, with a graph that builds as the answer is spoken. Voice is a Pro feature.

What's the difference between Trace It and voice?

Trace It turns a PR into a written, feature-by-feature walkthrough that you read at your own pace. Voice (Pro) gives you the walkthrough out loud, live, as soon as you ask, and lets you steer it by asking questions. They are separate features.

Can it keep up with many agents working in parallel?

It is built for that queue: for each PR, DiffGuardian finds the quickest way to help you understand it, whether that is a written walkthrough, a spoken one with the code highlighted, or a graph of what it touches. It speeds up understanding, you approve when you're ready, and it never merges anything.

I'm a PM, not an engineer. Is it for me?

Yes. Ask what a PR or your codebase does and get a plain-English answer out loud, with the code highlighted or a graph of the codebase alongside. You don't need to read code to follow it.

Is it only for solo developers?

No. A new developer can set up in a few minutes and talk to the codebase to learn how it works. The author, reviewer and PM can each get the walkthrough that suits them, and whoever inherits an agent-written PR can get it without waiting on the author.

Where does my voice go?

Straight from your machine to the provider you chose, using your own OpenAI or ElevenLabs key, or it stays with your operating system's built-in voice. Nothing reaches DiffGuardian's servers.

Is my code private?

Your code never reaches a DiffGuardian server. Reviews run on your own machine, and cloud reviews go directly from your machine to the provider whose key you supplied — under your own agreement with them. Because local models are supported on every plan, you can use the AI features without a single line of code leaving your laptop. See the

Security page for the full data-flow breakdown.

Which platforms is DiffGuardian available on?

DiffGuardian is available for macOS, Windows and Linux. The Windows build is an x64 installer that isn't code-signed yet, so Windows may show a SmartScreen warning before you can run it. On Linux, install the .deb or

.rpm package for your distribution — they declare the dependency DiffGuardian's secure key storage needs, so it works out of the box. Use the AppImage only if neither package fits your distribution; it still auto-updates like every other build.

How does billing work, and can I cancel?

seats. Cancel any time from the billing portal — you keep access until the end of the period you already paid for.

How is this different from the AI tools I already have?

DiffGuardian doesn't judge the code for you. It makes sure the person who approves understands it. See how DiffGuardian compares.

Trace It

Prefer to read? Trace It gives you the walkthrough at your pace.

Hit Trace It! and a 5,000-line PR becomes a guided tour, one feature at a time, each explained in plain English. Read it as slowly as you like, go back, and approve having seen the whole thing, not skimmed a diff.

Built for parallel agents

问题

Your questions, answered.

What does DiffGuardian actually do?

DiffGuardian helps engineers, PMs and anyone building software

understand code as fast as agents write it. It gives you a walkthrough of a pull request one feature at a time, lets you talk to a PR or your whole codebase and hear the answer, and leaves the decision to approve with you.

Can I really talk to a PR?

是的。 On the PR page, hold Space, ask, release, and hear the answer while the lines it discusses are highlighted. Analyze Project has the same push-to-talk in a full-screen overlay, with a graph that builds as the answer is spoken. Voice is a Pro feature.

What's the difference between Trace It and voice?

Trace It turns a PR into a written, feature-by-feature walkthrough that you read at your own pace. Voice (Pro) gives you the walkthrough out loud, live, as soon as you ask, and lets you steer it by asking questions. They are separate features.

Can it keep up with many agents working in parallel?

It is built for that queue: for each PR, DiffGuardian finds the quickest way to help you understand it, whether that is a written walkthrough, a spoken one with the code highlighted, or a graph of what it touches. It speeds up understanding, you approve when you're ready, and it never merges anything.

I'm a PM, not an engineer. Is it for me?

是的。 Ask what a PR or your codebase does and get a plain-English answer out loud, with the code highlighted or a graph of the codebase alongside. You don't need to read code to follow it.

Is it only for solo developers?

No. A new developer can set up in a few minutes and talk to the codebase to learn how it works. The author, reviewer and PM can each get the walkthrough that suits them, and whoever inherits an agent-written PR can get it without waiting on the author.

Where does my voice go?

Straight from your machine to the provider you chose, using your own OpenAI or ElevenLabs key, or it stays with your operating system's built-in voice. Nothing reaches DiffGuardian's servers.

Is my code private?

Your code never reaches a DiffGuardian server. Reviews run on your own machine, and cloud reviews go directly from your machine to the provider whose key you supplied — under your own agreement with them. Because local models are supported on every plan, you can use the AI features without a single line of code leaving your laptop. See the

Security page for the full data-flow breakdown.

Which platforms is DiffGuardian available on?

DiffGuardian is available for macOS, Windows and Linux. The Windows build is an x64 installer that isn't code-signed yet, so Windows may show a SmartScreen warning before you can run it. On Linux, install the .deb or

.rpm package for your distribution — they declare the dependency DiffGuardian's secure key storage needs, so it works out of the box. Use the AppImage only if neither package fits your distribution; it still auto-updates like every other build.
